sentences.text: 4. Also, the Petitioner has undertaken to pay a one-time compensation amount of Rs.20,000/- to the Respondent No. 2, who has, in turn, undertaken to cooperate in the quashing proceedings and has no objection to the quashing of the F.I.R bearing No. 301 of 2018.

5. Respondent No.2 is present before this Court and he submits that the Petitioner was no drunk on the date of the incident and no threat was extended by him and he has no objection to the quashing of the FIR in question.

6. This Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has inherent power to quash criminal proceedings even in those cases which are not compoundable, but such power has to be exercised sparingly and with great caution.
In the present case, the Complaint of the FIR has submitted that he was not extended any threat by the Petitioner and he has been duly compensated by the Petitioner.
